findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several items in storage areas throughout the facility used for cleaned dishes were observed with remaining food debris on them. The PIC was shown and moved the items back to the dish area for re-cleaning to correct. They are instructed to review with all dish washers acceptable levels of cleanliness for the food contact equipment and conduct oversight as needed to ensure that the dishes are cleaned appropriately at all times. Ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The hand sink in the bar area was observed pulling away from the wall which exposed a gap between the sink and the wall. The PIC was shown and instructed to reseal the sink to the wall prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all surfaces in the facility were maintained smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The fan cover in the back walk in cooler was observed with an accumulation of dust that has developed to the point where concerns include contamination of foods stored in the cooler. The PIC was instructed to clean the cover and maintain it clean moving forward. Ensure that all physical facilities are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet, therefore recontaminating their hands. The PIC was notified and instructed to review hand washing procedures with all staff. Ensure that the hand washing procedures in the facility protect freshly washed hands from recontamination.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing prior to food service/handling. Education was conducted and they are instructed to review hand washing with employees. Ensure that hand washing takes place at all times that it is required in the facility.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The two display coolers next to the ordering line were observed to be holding TCS foods with internal temperatures of 49F-51F. When discussing with the PIC the items in the coolers were mostly placed into these coolers the day before the inspection in the morning. The only exception were the cannolis which arrived in the cooler approximately 5 hours prior to the inspection. The TCS items observed include multiple containers of ricotta filling, parmesan cheese, roast beef and several slices of cheese cake. The cannolis were allowed to remain until 4pm (six hours) and then be discarded. The remaining TCS items were discarded immediately to correct the violation. The PICs cleaned the filters on the front and back of the coolers to hopefully fix the overall issue. They also stated that they had contacted the owners who were having a company come to ensure that a more in depth maintenance scenario was not needed. The violation is considered corrected at this time with the caveat that the inspector will return in the morning to check if the remedial actions taken during the inspection were sufficient. The PICs are aware that tomorrow’s visit could ensure violations requiring follow ups in the future.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

Two employee cell phones were observed on a counter used for food preparation. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the phones moved to correct the immediate violation. Ensure employee possessions are stored in locations where contamination of foods or food contact surfaces is not a concern.

6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

A spray bottle in the front of the facility is observed with a clear liquid and no label indicating its use. The PIC indicated that the bottle contains a premixed sanitizer. The PIC was instructed to label the bottle as sanitizer and did so to correct the violation. Ensure that all chemicals are labeled at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Multiple TCS foods are observed in the pizza prep cooler  in the front of the facility with internal temperatures ranging from 45F-50F. One item (fresh mozzarella) is observed with internal temperatures of 60F. A time control system will continue to be utilized until the prep cooler is functioning correctly, and the TCS items discarded every 6 hour (so long as they are maintained under 70F). Today’s batch of foods placed into the cooler were brought from the walk in cooler at approximately 10:30am and will be discarded at 4:30 pm. The violation is considered temporarily corrected, pursuant to line item #33 of this report.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. 

Two gallons of milk are observed in the walk in cooler approximately half used and without date marking. Two containers of half n’ half are also observed partially used and without date marking. The kitchen employee was unaware of when the containers were opened but believed it to be within the past couple of days. The containers were marked with the date two days ago to correct the immediate violation. This is the third inspection in a row where this situation has been noted. Educate staff on proper date marking procedures and endure that they are maintained moving forward.

findings.comment:

None of the employees at the facility during his inspection have an observable CFPM certificate. Hand outs were given to the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that sufficient CFPM’s are available to cover all shifts of operation.

A pan of raw sausage is observed on a shelf over Ready-To-Eat items (ham/pepperoni, ect.) in the walk in cooler. A date marking of yesterday (1/31) is observed on the pan. The kitchen manager was consulted and the pan moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. 

A mug with measuring scoops is observed with sharpie markers stored in it as well. Sharpies are not considered a clean item and should not be stored in contact with food contact items. After discussing with the kitchen manager the sharpies were removed and the measuring scoops moved to dish for cleaning. Maintain food contact utensils clean prior to use.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Food handler cards were not available for employees not having a CFPM certificate. The issue was discussed and the PIC is instructed to ensure that all food handlers have completed food handler training and copies of the certificates are maintained at the facility.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Verification of notice to report are not available at the time of this inspection. A copy of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreement was given to the PIC. A follow up will be conducted in two weeks for compliance.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

Procedures were not available for clean up of Vomit/Diarrheal events. A copy of the clean up procedure given out by this department was given during this inspection to correct. Body fluid clean up and blood clean up kits were discussed as alternatives. Ensure that a procedure is available for use at all times.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

A partially used gallon of milk is observed in the walk in cooler with a use by date of 10/17/23. The gallon is also without a date marking. PIC was consulted and the gallon discarded to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

A metal half pan is currently storing dough slicers. There is both a pen and a sharpie marker observed in the bottom of this container mixed in with the food contact surfaces. These are generally not considered clean surfaces that are safe to contact food contact surfaces. The PIC was consulted and the slicers moved to dish for cleaning. Do not store these items together.

The floor of the back walk in cooler appears to have dough build up that has not been recently cleaned. PIC was notified and instructed to maintain the floor clean throughout the facility.
